full_judgment: 11. It was next contended by the learned lawyer appearing for accused appellant, Saleh Ahmed Master and also by Mr. S C. Das. the learned Counsel appearing for the accused-appellant, Aminul Islam that the whole trial was vitiated by misjoinder of charges and illegal joint trial and that having regard to the fact that the alleged offences were distinct and separate offences punishable under two distinct and different sets of laws they could not he joined together and tried at one trial We, however do not find any sub, lance in this contention also. Section 235 (1&2) Cr.P.C read with section 239(d) Cr.P C provided that persons accused of different and distinct offences but committed in the course of same transaction and the acts so committed if falls within two or mare separate definitions of any law by which offences are defined and punished persons accused of them may be charged and tried at one trial for each of such offences. Though punishable under two different sets of laws (ref 7 DLR 566; 25 DLR (14), committed In course of the same transaction, convicted and sentenced subject to section 71 of the Penal Code, under one law only as when one act constitutes two offences punishment for each can be inflicted if both the offences are against the same law and not against different laws. (ref 18 Cr.L J. 321. 1916 AIR.  Punjab. 86) The real test by which to determine whether several distinct offences are so connected as to form the same transaction depends on whether they ate so related to one another in point of purpose or as cause and effect or as principle and subsidiary acts as to constitute one continuous action of a continuous whole.
